critique.good: The five prayer columns are all 68px, so they read as one uniform band of like values; every time has 47px of content space and never touches a border, and all five headers fit with slack.
critique.problems: The row identifier is the most cramped element in the table: the header المدينة (49px) sits in 52px of content, nearly touching its borders, and مكة المكرمة / المدينة المنورة break into two lines, pushing rows 2–3 to 60px and destroying the row rhythm a column-wise scan depends on.
critique.cause: Giving all five time columns the same 68px — the minimum forced by the 47px المغرب header — leaves only 73px for col 1, i.e. 52px of text against a 49px longest word.

critique.good: Every cell is on one line, all rows are a uniform 36px, the table is 46px shorter than the others, and no header wraps; the widths are content-minimal (35/35/38/47/41 header + 21 padding = exactly 56/56/59/68/62).
critique.problems: There is no breathing room: the clock values sit flush against the cell borders, and the band is visibly unequal — المغرب at 68px is 12px wider than الفجر and الظهر at 56px, so one prayer column looks more important than the rest.
critique.cause: Allocating 112px to col 1 (exactly the 91px one-line city width + padding) consumes all the slack, leaving precisely the 301px the five header minimums demand and nothing to distribute.

critique.good: The 91px city column gives the wrapped compound names room, and the two-line rows are at least consistent (rows 2 and 3 both 60px) so the wrap reads as a decision rather than an accident.
critique.problems: 91px (70px content) is an unhappy middle: too narrow for the 91px one-line city name, far wider than the 49px longest word, so the extra space buys nothing while the time columns go without. The band is also uneven for no content reason (60,60,62,70,70): المغرب and العشاء get 8–10px more than الفجر/الظهر, implying a hierarchy that does not exist.
critique.cause: The city column was set just past its longest word instead of either exactly at it or at the full one-line width, and the remaining 322px were handed out without reference to the header widths 35/35/38/47/41.

critique.good: The city column is clearly the widest (79px), so the row identifier separates cleanly from the data block; all six headers stay on one line, no mid-word splits, and the five prayer columns read as a single band.
critique.problems: The prayer band is uniformly too generous: العشاء carries 68px for a 41px header (27px dead space) and الفجر 66px for 35px, while the city column still cannot hold مكة المكرمة or المدينة المنورة on one line. The two-line city names break into lines of very unequal length, so those two rows look lopsided inside their 60px blocks, and the time figures float in air rather than sitting in a tight band.
critique.cause: Slack was spent on the short-header prayer columns (66–68px each) instead of on col 1; col 1's 79px (58px content) is 33px short of the 91px needed for one-line city names.

critique.good: The most regular of the three: every prayer column is 68px, so the five time columns form a perfectly even band, headers unwrapped, and no row looks structurally different from another.
critique.problems: The hierarchy is inverted: the row identifier is the narrowest-ish column at 72px (51px content) against a 49px longest unbreakable word, leaving ~2px of side margin, so المدينة المنورة nearly touches both cell edges and the wrapped city names look crammed. Meanwhile العشاء (41px needed) sits in 68px of space. The column that a reader uses first is the one that looks squeezed.
critique.cause: Fixed equal widths of 68–69px for all five prayer columns force col 1 down to the residual 72px, just above the hard 49px word minimum.

critique.good: The strongest of the three: col 1 gets the most width (84px), and tightening the prayer columns to 65/65/64/69/66 pulls the numbers into a visibly tighter band that reads as one group of like values.
critique.problems: The slack inside the band is uneven: المغرب at 69px sits only 1px above its 68px minimum, so its header looks pinched against the cell borders, while الفجر and الظهر at 65px each have 9px of air. The eye reads المغرب as cramped and the neighbouring columns as loose, which breaks the uniform band the design is aiming for; the city names still wrap.
critique.cause: Prayer widths were chosen by eye per column rather than as (column minimum + a constant buffer), so the buffers vary from 1px to 9px.

critique.good: The only layout where the grid stays perfectly regular: all seven rows are 36px, every header and every time value is on one line, no mid-word breaks, and the city column at 112px is wide enough for المدينة المنورة to sit on a single line. That width also does the job the brief asks of column 1 — at nearly double a prayer column it clearly separates the row identifier from the five-value time band, and because the five prayer columns are narrow and equal-ish in feel, the eye sweeps left across a continuous strip of clock times.
critique.problems: Everything is flush to its limit: the header المغرب (47px) exactly fills its 47px of content space, العصر (38) exactly fills 38, and المدينة المنورة (91) exactly fills 91. Nothing has a single pixel of slack, so the band looks slightly pinched next to the generous city column, and the layout is brittle — a font-rendering or rounding difference of 1px would push a header or a city name onto a second line.
critique.cause: col 1 = 112px is precisely the one-line width of the longest city name (91 + 21 padding). That leaves 301px for the five prayer columns, which is exactly the sum of their minimum widths (56+56+59+68+62). There is zero slack anywhere in the table.

critique.good: Buys real breathing room for the time columns — الفجر/الظهر get 58 instead of 56, المغرب 70 instead of 68 — so values like 11:56 and 12:24 sit comfortably rather than edge to edge, and مكة المكرمة still holds one line.
critique.problems: One row (المدينة المنورة) collapses to two lines and grows to 60px, producing a single tall row in a stack of 36px rows. It reads as an accident rather than a decision: the vertical rhythm of the table breaks exactly where the eye is scanning down the city list, and the data cells beside it become a large empty box, which visually over-weights that one city.
critique.cause: col 1 = 102px gives only 81px of text, below the ~85–91px needed by المدينة المنورة, so it wraps. The 10px taken from the city column were spread over five prayer columns as 2–4px each — a gain too small to notice, paid for with a 24px taller row.

critique.good: The five prayer columns are the most comfortable of the three (60, 60, 63, 72, 66), so headers and times never feel pinched, and the gain is spread evenly across the band rather than concentrated in one column.
critique.problems: Two rows (مكة المكرمة and المدينة المنورة) are 60px while the other five are 36px, and they sit adjacent, creating an irregular block in the middle of the table. Wrapped city names also destroy the city column's function as a scannable list of six place names — the reader has to re-read two entries as phrases instead of recognising them at a glance. Table height grows from 255 to 301px for a gain of only 4px in the widest column.
critique.cause: col 1 = 92px gives 71px of text, below the width of both two-word city names, so both wrap; the 20px released were handed to the prayer columns, which were already adequate at their minimums.

r0A.idea: Democratic grid: one narrow row-header column that lets long city names wrap, and five identical time columns so no prayer looks more important than another.

r0B.idea: City-first: spend almost all slack on a wide row header that keeps every city on one line, and squeeze each time column to its exact header minimum.

r0C.idea: Two-tier: a one-line city column at its natural width, tight columns for the three daytime prayers, and slightly airier columns for the evening pair (المغرب، العشاء) that close the row.

r1A.idea: Takes 2px from each of الفجر/الظهر/العصر in r0A (66 still clears their 59–62px header minimums) and hands the 6px to the city column, 73→79, giving المدينة 58px of content and its words real slack. The band stays effectively uniform (a 2px step is invisible) while every time keeps 45–47px, and no header is within 2px of wrapping.

r1B.idea: Keeps r0A's perfectly uniform 68px band, sends the single spare pixel to العشاء (the widest header after المغرب), and trims the city column to 72px — still 51px of content against a 49px longest word. Maximum air and rhythm for the time values, minimum but legal room for the city names; the tightest of the uniform-band options.

r1C.idea: Commits openly to two-line city names: a genuinely wide row-header column (63px content) so المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة break at the space into balanced halves with air around them, and a band that varies by only 5px (44/44/43/48/45px of content) instead of r0C's arbitrary 8–10px jumps. Trades the 36px row rhythm for a comfortable identifier and comfortable numbers at the same time.

r2A.idea: Every column gets exactly its measured one-line width (col 1 91+21=112, then 56/56/59/68/62 = the exact minimums of الفجر/الظهر/العصر/المغرب/العشاء). Result: no cell wraps anywhere — المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة sit on one line, all seven rows collapse to a uniform 36px height, and the table becomes a compact 252px grid instead of 301px with two 60px rows. Col 1 at 112px also gives the row identifier the visual weight it needs. Slack is zero, so this is the exact-fit design: any 1–2px measurement error in a bold header would cause a wrap.

r2B.idea: Same minimum-plus-constant-buffer logic but with a 2px buffer on each prayer column (56+2, 56+2, 59+2, 68+2, 62+2) and the remaining 102px to col 1. This removes r1C's 1px pinch on المغرب and its 9px looseness on الفجر/الظهر — all five columns now breathe equally — while col 1 reaches 81px of content, enough for مكة المكرمة on one line and only المدينة المنورة wrapping.

r2C.idea: A 4px buffer on every prayer column (60/60/63/72/66) makes the band maximally even and comfortable, at the cost of col 1 dropping to 92px (71px content), so the two longest city names wrap to two lines. This is the direct fix of r1C: identical buffers instead of 1–9px variation, a wider city column, and no column that looks pinched.

contrast.idea: Equal-width columns ignore the row-header role: the city column gets only 47px of content, below the 49px longest unbreakable word, so city names break mid-word or wrap repeatedly while the prayer columns receive unnecessary width. This destroys the hierarchy and makes the rows much harder to scan.

understanding.purpose: A quick-reference timetable of daily prayer times for six Saudi cities: readers look up one city's day, or compare one prayer across cities.
understanding.reading: Right-to-left: the eye lands on the city name (row header) first, then sweeps left across the five prayer times; the dominant comparison is column-wise (same prayer across cities), with row-wise reading as the secondary mode.
groups: col 1 (المدينة) is the row identifier and must be visually separated from the data block
cols 2–6 (الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء) are five instances of the same kind of value — clock times — and should read as one uniform band, with no column appearing more important than another
keep_intact: every time value, e.g. 8:16, 12:24, 3:23 — they must never wrap or break at the colon
the single-word headers الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء, which cannot wrap and set each column's minimum width
may_wrap: city names, especially المدينة المنورة (two words) and مكة المكرمة — wrapping them to a second line is harmless because the row height already accommodates two lines

bad.why: Equal-width columns ignore the row-header role: the city column gets only 47px of content, below the 49px longest unbreakable word, so city names break mid-word or wrap repeatedly while the prayer columns receive unnecessary width. This destroys the hierarchy and makes the rows much harder to scan.

contrast.why: Equal-width columns ignore the row-header role: the city column gets only 47px of content, below the 49px longest unbreakable word, so city names break mid-word or wrap repeatedly while the prayer columns receive unnecessary width. This destroys the hierarchy and makes the rows much harder to scan.

final.rationale: r0B and r2A are the same allocation and the only one that keeps all six city names and all prayer times on one line at 15px. The 112px city column is correctly the widest because it is the row header; the prayer columns are sized to their own headers, with Fajr/Dhuhr narrowest and Maghrib widest. Uniform 36px rows make each city read as a single horizontal unit and keep the table compact at 255px. The remaining designs are publishable but trade compactness for two-line city names and uneven row heights.

general: Size a row-header/identifier column to its longest label, not to the width of the data columns.
Columns that share a role can be narrow and near-equal, but each must still fit its own header and longest unbreakable content.
Uniform row heights and one-line cells improve vertical scanning; extra width should go to the column that actually needs it.
A table that exactly fills its container is efficient but brittle: it leaves no tolerance for longer labels.
specific: In this Arabic RTL table the city column needs at least 112px to keep المدينة المنورة on one line: 91px one-line width plus 21px padding.
The prayer-column minima are 56, 56, 59, 68 and 62px because their headers are the widest content; the minima sum to exactly 413px, so there is no spare width.
Fajr and Dhuhr are the narrowest prayer columns, while Maghrib is widest because المغرب is wider than the other prayer headers.
Wrapping city names but never prayer times is readable, but it makes rows uneven and weakens the city labels as row anchors.

final.tradeoffs: r0B is maximally compact but has zero slack, so any longer city name would force a wrap; a designer might prefer r2B's wider city column and accept one two-line row. Another reasonable disagreement is whether two-line city names are acceptable in exchange for slightly wider prayer columns, as in r0C, r1A, r1B and r1C.
final.uncertain: Whether r0B's exact-fit columns feel too cramped in practice, whether r2B's single wrapped row is the better compromise, and whether the identical r0B/r2A pair should count as two preferences or one.

A.why: Column 1 is far too narrow: «مكة المكرمة» breaks mid-word into three lines («مكة / المكرم / ة»), which is a serious typographic error in Arabic; «المدينة المنورة» also wraps, and the tall rows make the grid ragged.

B.why: No broken words and all times sit on one line, but the time columns carry slack while column 1 is squeezed so «المدينة المنورة» wraps to two lines, leaving rows 2–3 visibly taller than the rest.

C.why: Column 1 is sized just enough for the longest city name on one line, and the five time columns are proportioned to their headers (المغرب widest, الفجر/الظهر narrower). Every row is a single line, row heights are even, and the header band reads as one clean unit.

D.why: Same defect as A: the row-header column is too narrow, splitting «المكرمة» across lines («المكرم / ة») and wrapping other names, so rows no longer read as units and heights jump.

E.why: Words stay intact, but column 1 is still short of the full city name so «المدينة المنورة» wraps, and the time columns are wide with unused space; the result is uneven row rhythm (rows 2–3 much taller).

F.why: All city names and all times fit on one line, giving uniform row heights; header widths match their content (المغرب widest, الفجر narrowest) and the first column reads clearly as a row-header band.

reviews.unsure: A and D look nearly identical in width distribution, so I could not separate them; the exact column-1 widths in B/E and the tiny differences between C and F are hard to measure by eye.

A.why: The city column is disproportionately wide yet 'مكة المكرمة' breaks into three lines, splitting 'المكرمة' into 'المكرم'/'ة'; rows 2–3 become tall and disrupt the row rhythm.

B.why: Same problem as A: awkward three-line break inside 'المكرمة' and uneven row heights, despite the city column taking far more width than the time columns.

C.why: Time columns are balanced and readable; 'مكة المكرمة' stays on one line and 'المدينة المنورة' wraps cleanly at the word boundary, though that one row is taller.

D.why: Similar to C: clean word-boundary wrapping and even time columns; one taller city row is acceptable, though the city column could be slightly more generous.

E.why: All city names fit on one line, including 'المدينة المنورة'; time columns remain legible, rows are uniform, and the wider city column is justified as the row-header column.

F.why: Like E, it avoids broken words and uneven rows: every city name stays intact, time columns are consistent, and the hierarchy of row headers versus time data is clear.

reviews.unsure: A/B appear visually identical, and C/D and E/F are very close; without exact pixel widths I may be over-weighting small differences, especially the extra width in the city column versus the time columns.
